<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Anyayogavyavacchedikādvātriṁśikā Kāvya is a Sanskrit poem written by Hemacandra, a renowned Jain scholar, poet, and polymath who lived in India during the 12th century CE. The poem is part of the shat-khandagama, one of the most important Jain scriptures, and is a commentary on the second chapter of the text, which deals with the concept of injustice.<br>Anyayogavyavacchedikādvātriṁśikā Kāvya is notable for its intricate use of language, complex rhetorical devices, and poetic style. It contains 32 verses, each of which is structured in the form of a doha, a type of couplet commonly used in Hindi poetry. The poem is written in the style of kāvya, a classical Sanskrit literary genre characterized by its ornate language, complex structure, and elevated style. Anyayogavyavacchedikādvātriṁśikā Kāvya is also known for its philosophical content, as it discusses the nature of injustice and the ways in which it can be overcome through the practice of Jainism. It emphasizes the importance of non-violence, compassion, and self-control, and argues that true justice can only be achieved through the cultivation of these qualities.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Anyayogavyavacchedikādvātriṁśikā Kāvya&quot; consists of 32 verses that describe the tenets of the Jain philosophy of non-absolutism, also known as Anekāntavāda. The work is written in the form of poetry, making it both aesthetically pleasing and easy to remember. Each verse is composed in the Arya meter, with sixteen syllables in each line. The text explains the concept of Syādvāda or &quot;theory of conditioned predication&quot; that advocates that truth is relative and depends on the viewpoint of the observer. The work argues that all viewpoints are partial and limited and that the absolute truth is beyond human comprehension. It also discusses the concept of Nayavāda or &quot;the doctrine of partial viewpoints,&quot; which asserts that all knowledge is partial and that no single viewpoint can encompass the entire reality.<br>The verses of the text explain the significance of non-absolutism in the Jain worldview and how it can help people to coexist peacefully with those who have different beliefs and perspectives. The text also highlights the importance of tolerance, compassion, and nonviolence in human life. The work also provides an overview of the history and development of the Jain religion and its principles. It references various Jain scriptures and the lives of Jain Tīrthaṅkara, the spiritual leaders of Jainism, to illustrate its arguments.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Anyayogavyavacchedikādvātriṁśikā Kāvya&quot; is a unique work in Sanskrit literature due to its satirical and humorous style. The poem uses a light-hearted and witty approach to criticize the flaws and absurdities in the social, political, and religious systems of the time. Hemacandra employs various literary devices such as puns, paradoxes, and exaggerations to create a playful yet thought-provoking work that challenges the norms and conventions of society. The work's novelty lies in its ability to convey serious social commentary through an entertaining and engaging literary form.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Anyayogavyavacchedikādvātriṁśikā Kāvya&quot; is considered to be one of the most significant works of Hemacandra in Sanskrit literature. It is a remarkable piece of writing that has contributed immensely to the development of poetry and literature in Sanskrit. This work is highly valued for its unique and innovative style, as well as for the depth of its content. Hemacandra's use of satire and irony to criticize social and religious norms was a departure from the traditional approaches to writing poetry and literature. The work highlights the importance of rational thinking, critical inquiry, and the pursuit of truth in a society dominated by dogmatism and superstition. Moreover, it reflects Hemacandra's own values and philosophy, emphasizing the need for ethical and moral conduct in individuals and society. The work has been studied and appreciated by scholars and poets for centuries and has inspired many other writers in the Sanskrit literary tradition.<br>Thus, &quot;Anyayogavyavacchedikādvātriṁśikā Kāvya&quot; holds a significant place in the Sanskrit literary tradition, representing the zenith of Hemacandra's creative genius and his contribution to the development of poetry, literature, and philosophy in Sanskrit.<br><br>&quot;Anyayogavyavacchedikādvātriṁśikā Kāvya&quot; is a unique work that combines poetry with philosophy, addressing the issues of injustice and oppression prevalent in society. Hemacandra's use of metaphors and similes makes the text highly imaginative and thought-provoking.<br><br>The work has been translated into various Indian languages, including Hindi, Bengali, and Gujarati, and has been influential in shaping the Indian literary and philosophical tradition. It is considered one of the greatest works of Hemacandra and is highly regarded for its literary and philosophical value.</div></div></div>
